title: Python Multiline Strings
learningObjectives: Create strings that span multiple source-code lines.
Use triple single quotes and triple double quotes correctly.
Preserve and inspect newline characters in string values.
Distinguish multiline string literals from comments and docstrings.
Choose readable string construction techniques for longer text.

understand.concept: A multiline string is a string value whose source representation spans more than one line. Python supports triple single-quoted and triple double-quoted string literals for this purpose. Newline characters inside the literal become part of the string. Triple-quoted strings are still string objects; they are not block comments. A string in the first statement position of a module, class or function body can serve as a docstring.
understand.whyItMatters: Multiline strings are useful for messages, descriptions, templates and text data that would be difficult to read as one long source line. Knowing how newlines are represented helps control output and file content.
understand.analogy: A multiline string is like a note written on several lines of a page, with the line breaks preserved when the note is read.
understand.analogyLimit: Triple quotes do not automatically format arbitrary data safely for HTML, SQL or shell commands. They only define a Python string; output still needs context-appropriate handling.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Triple-quoted literals

Use three single quotes (`'''`) or three double quotes (`"""`) to write a string across multiple source lines. Both forms create ordinary string values. Choose a delimiter that avoids unnecessary escaping inside the text.

## 2. Newline characters

Physical line breaks inside a triple-quoted literal are included in the resulting string as newline characters. The `\n` escape sequence can also represent a newline inside a regular quoted string. Use `print()` to display the lines.

## 3. Indentation and whitespace

Whitespace inside a multiline literal is part of the string. If the source code is indented, those spaces may also become part of the value. Be deliberate about indentation when building text that must match exactly.

## 4. Strings are not comments

A triple-quoted expression creates a string object. Python uses a string literal as a docstring when it appears in the first statement position of a module, class or function body. An arbitrary triple-quoted string elsewhere is not a special block comment.

## 5. Choose a clear representation

Use adjacent string literals, explicit newline escapes or triple-quoted strings according to readability and the exact whitespace required by the output.

examples.title: Create a multiline message
examples.code:
message = '''Hello, learner!
Welcome to Python.
Keep practising.'''
print(message)
examples.expectedOutput:
Hello, learner!
Welcome to Python.
Keep practising.
examples.explanation: The triple single quotes allow the string to span three source lines, and the newline characters are preserved.

examples.title: Use triple double quotes
examples.code:
notice = """Library hours:
Monday to Friday
9 AM to 5 PM"""
print(notice)
examples.expectedOutput:
Library hours:
Monday to Friday
9 AM to 5 PM
examples.explanation: Triple double quotes provide the same multiline string capability as triple single quotes.

examples.title: Use an explicit newline escape
examples.explanation: The escape sequence \n inserts a newline into a normal single-quoted string.

examples.title: Count lines in a multiline string
examples.code:
poem = '''Rain falls
Wind blows
Sun returns'''
print(len(poem.splitlines()))
examples.explanation: splitlines() separates the string at line boundaries, and len() counts the resulting lines.

examples.title: Distinguish a string from a docstring
examples.code:
def course_name():
    """Return the course title."""
    return 'Python'

print(course_name.__doc__)
examples.explanation: The first string literal in the function body is its docstring and is available through the __doc__ attribute.

practise.guidedTask: Create a three-line welcome message using triple quotes. Print it and count the number of lines with splitlines().
practise.independentTask: Write a multiline event announcement containing a title, date and location. Make sure the output has exactly the intended line breaks and no accidental leading spaces.
hints: Use three matching quote characters to open and close the literal.

Use splitlines() to work with individual lines.

A triple-quoted string is not automatically a comment.
practise.challenge: Create a multiline receipt with item, quantity and total fields. Use f-strings or a clear string-building approach, then verify the exact output including spaces and line breaks.

questions.prompt: Which syntax creates a multiline string literal?
options: Triple single or triple double quotes
Only // at the start of each line
questions.answer: Triple single or triple double quotes
questions.explanation: Python supports both triple single-quoted and triple double-quoted string literals.

questions.prompt: Are line breaks inside a triple-quoted string part of the string value?
questions.explanation: Newline characters inside the literal are included in the resulting string.

questions.prompt: What does the escape sequence \n represent?
questions.explanation: The \n escape sequence represents a line break in a string.

questions.prompt: Is every triple-quoted string a Python block comment?
options: No, it is a string literal
Yes, Python ignores all triple quotes
Only if it contains two lines
questions.answer: No, it is a string literal
questions.explanation: Triple-quoted text is a string. A docstring is a string in a specific first-statement position.

questions.prompt: How can a function's docstring be accessed?
questions.explanation: The __doc__ attribute stores the function's docstring when one is defined.
